findings.title: `SDKExecutionSession.auto_memory` assumes `base_options.env` is never None
findings.description: `auto_memory` does `AUTO_MEMORY_DISABLE_ENV not in self.base_options.env`. Every production builder (`open_pipeline_session`, used by both `cli/commands/run.py:348` and the executor's lazy connect) always sets `env` via `sdk_settings_options`, and the sibling `setting_sources` property explicitly tolerates `None` — so `env` is the one option field this dataclass's invariants leave implicit. The test fake `tests/pipeline/conftest.py::scripted_session` builds `ClaudeAgentOptions(cwd=".", permission_mode="bypassPermissions")` with no `env`, and if any test or future builder ever reaches `session.auto_memory` on such an object it raises `TypeError` rather than answering. One line hardens the invariant: `return AUTO_MEMORY_DISABLE_ENV not in (self.base_options.env or {})`. No current production or test path trips this, hence NOTE.

findings.title: `default_system_prompt_preset_used` → `system_prompt_mode` rename: residual readers not fully verifiable
findings.description: The diff removes `ReviewResult.default_system_prompt_preset_used` and updates all in-diff consumers (`review/models.py`, `review/persistence.py`'s `_PRESET_MODES` check, `review/review_client.py`, and the test suite). I verified the persistence code handles `None` safely (`None in _PRESET_MODES` is `False`) and that `to_dict()` emits the new keys. However, I could not exhaustively grep the repository for any out-of-diff reader of the old attribute name (e.g., save-targets, frontmatter consumers, or tooling that reads hand-built results). If one exists it would now `AttributeError` at runtime; if the test suite passes, this is a non-issue — flagging only for the record since the hunk evidence alone can't prove absence.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` exceeds the ~300-line guideline
findings.description: The file is now ~470 lines after absorbing the idle-timeout, reconnect-usability, and settings-policy logic. The slice did the right structural move — pure turn bookkeeping went to `sdk_turns.py` and settings to `providers/sdk/settings.py` — and the remainder is one cohesive lifecycle class, so the guideline's "where practical" applies; noting it so a future slice can consider moving the dispatch/turn-reading block (`dispatch`, `_collect_turns`, `_read_turn_with_retry`, `_read_turn`) into a companion module if the file keeps growing.

findings.title: Failure modes are observable and test-covered with the new code
findings.description: Verified against the implementation: (1) idle-timeout while waiting on background agents logs a WARNING naming the agents and records `background_tasks_stopped` (`test_silence_while_waiting_stops_agents_and_returns`, `test_stop_task_failure_is_logged_and_next_id_still_stopped`); (2) foreground turns are explicitly timer-free and a test asserts the config read never happens (`test_slow_foreground_turn_has_no_timer`); (3) a failed rotation reconnect marks the session unusable, ERROR-logs with traceback, and later items are flagged rather than silently re-queried (`test_items_after_failed_reconnect_are_flagged_unusable` asserts the fresh client's `query` is never called); (4) a leftover injected follow-up turn is discarded with a WARNING carrying its final text (`test_leftover_injected_turn_is_dropped_and_logged`); (5) stream-end with active agents fails with a named `ProviderError` (`test_stream_end_with_agent_tracked_raises`); (6) subagent prose is excluded from the response (`test_subagent_prose_is_not_part_of_the_response`); (7) the D7 final-text tail flows into both executor-level and `each`-batch flag reasons, asserted end-to-end in `test_executor.py` and `test_executor_each.py`. This matches the failure-mode enumeration rule: each path has a log/metadata signal and a test asserting it.
